title: Wagon cup holder: v9.1, longer reach to the strut
subtitle: Ring on the side rail + a C-grip on the angled strut whose closed wall faces the cup · no screw · a full cup pushes the grip on tighter · shown assembled in its real orientation (rail left to right) · millimetres

meshes.label: Clip (ring on rail + grip on strut; pops off)
LEFT-side clip (mirror image; shown on the same rail for comparison)
Angled strut (13.5 mm square, nominal gap 5.5 mm)

scale_note: Real size, shown assembled in its real orientation: the rail runs left to right, the cup stands upright and hangs off the outside of it. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube; the angled strut is your 13.5 mm square bar, drawn as a straight line at ~59° from the tape photos (so it is accurate to roughly a few mm). The gap between the rail and the strut is the least certain number (4 to 7 mm, drawn at 5.5). The tumbler is from retailer listings. The wireframe blocks are the red latch zones (approximate).
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v9.1: the strut grip was so tight it snapped when you fitted it. As you suggested, the big dovetail clip now sits further in on its bar (in the middle of the clear stretch) and the grip attaches much further down the strut, about 73 mm below the bar instead of 43, on a long vertical post. I also took stress out of the grip: 1.5 mm of extra room on the cup side (the cup's weight presses the strut onto that wall anyway), 0.4 mm clearance and shallower 1.2 mm lips. Both the right and left clips change (the module doesn't). Both need supports under the post and grip. Please check: (1) the post and grip look right on the strut (turn on the strut wireframe); (2) which step feels tight when you try it: the grip going onto the strut, or the ring going onto the bar? (3) print the new grip test (lips 1.2 / 1.6 / 2.0) if you want to tune the lips.
